transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ruth Patel (CTO, Sable Health), Ivan Gomez (SRE), Leah Brooks (PM), Samir Rao (Security), Speaker 6

Summary:
Quick sync to review pilot telemetry, agree a staged chaos/dry-run plan for cutover, finalize canary pass/fail signals, and record immediate action items. Focus on safety gates, rollback triggers, and what to measure during the canary windows.

Topics covered:
- Recent pilot telemetry and anomalies (token latency spikes during long sessions)
- Canary definitions for A/B traffic and progressive ramping
- Cutover runbook structure (preflight, safety window, rollback)
- Chaos testing in staging (cache eviction, node kill, KV cash miss sim)
- Compliance/security signoffs (KMS, audit logs, retention)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, everyone thanks for taking time. Quick roll call, and then we'll dive in. Diego is with me from the SE team. Ruth, you got it?
[00:05] Ruth Patel: Yep, hi hi, Ruth here. Ivan on SRE, Leah and Samir also on.
[00:09] Diego Alvarez: Hey everybody. I forwarded the staging telemetry doc this morning, there were a couple of interesting spikes I want to call out.
[00:14] Ivan Gomez: saw those, yeah. The 10/28 run had a couple of mid-session latency blips, looked related to cache thrash when we hit a rare prompt pattern.
[00:22] Maya Chen: OK, perfect. Diego, can you summarize what that looked like and whether it's something the runtime would fallback on?
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: Sure. So the runtime fallback kicked in for one shard — the system re-routed to a lower-capacity variant which increased token latency by about 280 ms for about two minutes. It didn't error, but you can see the delta in the per-token SLA. In our logs it's labeled as a KV cache miss but the transcriber sometimes writes it as "K V cash" which is fun.
[00:45] Leah Brooks: When you say fallback, is that the hosted variant or a cheaper quantized model? We need to flag whether quality regressed.
[00:52] Diego Alvarez: Good question. It fell back to the smaller quantized instance we had configured for burst. Quality delta was measurable but within the tolerance we agreed on, roughly a 3% drop on BLEU-ish scoring for the regen set.
[01:04] Ruth Patel: For us, anything over 5% quality drop is a blocker. Also latency > 300 ms on critical user flows is a blocker.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Noted. That's exactly why today's focus is the canary pass/fail signals and the chaos test plan. We want to practice the failure modes before the cutover.
[01:19] Samir Rao: From security, we need to confirm the audit logs will persist through the fallback, and that the KMS keys are accessible in the dedciated VPC. Also, who's managing the HSM?
[01:29] Maya Chen: For the Private mode customers, Redwood's integration supports customer-managed KMS; for this POC you're on a VPC peered setup with our control plane. Diego, can you state whether audit logs are preserved for fallback routes?
[01:38] Diego Alvarez: Audit events are emitted by the control plane regardless of runtime variant. The only caveat is if the control-plane-to-storage link is degraded — then there's a lag in log shipping. But we can configure longer retention on the local buffer; I'll include that in the runbook.
[01:50] Ivan Gomez: Good to know. For the chaos test, we're going to simulate a node kill and a KV cache eviction during mid-session to reproduce that 10/28 blip. I want Diego to define the exact traffic shape he'll use.
[01:59] Diego Alvarez: Plan is: 1) steady-state traffic at 70% of peak, 2) inject a 30-second cache eviction, 3) spike to 120% for 90 seconds, 4) observe reroute and latency. We'll run that in staging and watch the telemetry.
[02:12] Leah Brooks: And the acceptance criteria for the canary? Do we want zero user-facing errors or do we allow a small error rate?
[02:18] Maya Chen: Historically the POC acceptance we've seen: error rate < 0.5%, latency increase < 20% for 95th percentile, and quality degradation < 5% on our prompt set. But Ruth, you gave a tighter latency threshold — 300 ms on critical flows — so we'll set that as a firm gate for your critical routes.
[02:35] Ruth Patel: Yes, critical flows must stay under 300 ms p95. Non-critical can be looser.
[02:39] Diego Alvarez: We'll tag routes in the Router config so the canary only directs a small % of traffic for critical routes. Proposed canary ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 30 minutes with automated stop on signal.
[02:51] Ivan Gomez: What are the automated stop signals? CPU/GPU saturation, error rate, latency? Need explicit metrics and thresholds.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: Suggested signals: 1) p95 latency exceeds baseline by 40% or absolute p95 > 300 ms for critical routes; 2) error rate > 0.5% over a 2-minute window; 3) model quality regression based on automated evals exceeding 5% delta. Any one of those triggers an automated rollback.
[03:14] Leah Brooks: How fast is automated rollback? We need an SLA on time to revert to baseline — like 60s or 2 minutes?
[03:19] Diego Alvarez: The orchestrator can flip traffic within ~30-90 seconds depending on routing caches; we should plan for a worst-case 2 minutes. We'll document that in the runbook.
[03:26] Samir Rao: Legal asked about data residency during fallback. If traffic routes to a different region variant do we stay within the same data boundary?
[03:33] Maya Chen: Yes — routing respects region policies. For Sable Health we'll ensure any fallback is to an approved region/model variant. If capacity would force another region, the control plane will not reroute across region boundaries for your account.
[03:43] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[03:45] Maya Chen: Okay, moving on. Diego, can you talk about the dry-run schedule and what we need from Sable to make it representative?
[03:51] Diego Alvarez: Two parts: preflight rehearsal and full dry-run. Preflight is a checklist: baseline telemetry snapshot, traffic shaping config, secret/key validation, runbook readout. Full dry-run is a staged flip of non-critical traffic, then critical traffic after we validate metrics. For a realistic test we need a copy of production traffic or a faithful replay. If you can't provide full replay, we can synthesize traffic with the same session length distribution and prompt mix.
[04:15] Ivan Gomez: We can do a sanitized replay for staging, but timelines are tight. I can export a 24-hour window of production and scrub PHI, but need guidance on scrubbing.
[04:24] Samir Rao: Security will approve the scrub process; we'll need a list of fields to remove and a signed attestation. Maya, can you share Redwood's data handling doc?
[04:32] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll attach the data handling and SOC2 summary to the CRM.
[04:36] Ruth Patel: For the rollback playbook, I want explicit human escalation steps. If automated rollback fails, who is paged and what are the manual steps?
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: Good call. The runbook will include a manual rollback section: 1) invoke emergency cutover via the control plane UI; 2) DNS and LB rollback steps; 3) escalate to Redwood on-call. We'll include links and runbook anchors.
[04:57] Leah Brooks: Who's on Redwood on-call during the dry-run? We need a direct line.
[05:01] Maya Chen: Diego will be primary SE for the dry-run and we'll have a rotation; I'll include the on-call contact.
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: Also, a note on observability — please ensure you have the sampling keys for trace spans. If you're using our SDK we add trace IDs that flow through the runtime; that'll help root-cause the cache thrash.
[05:18] Ivan Gomez: We use DataDog for traces; can Redwood push spans into our APM or do we need to federate?
[05:24] Diego Alvarez: We support span export to OTLP; so you can ingest into DataDog or any OTLP-compatible backend. We'll add instructions to the telemetry doc.
[05:32] Ruth Patel: OK next: A/B test plan. Leah, you wanted to keep an evaluation matrix for user-visible metrics and automated evals, right?
[05:39] Leah Brooks: Yes. The plan is to run A/B for 7 days on a subset of users with automated evals on the prompt set — we need a daily quality report and a regression alert. Also need to know cost delta for serving on the new model variant.
[05:51] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize can provide a cost delta estimate for the proposed batch/caching settings. We'll run an optimized config for the new variant to get a realistic cost projection.
[06:00] Ruth Patel: Cost is a big factor — if the new variant raises unit cost > 12% we need to justify by improved latency or quality.
[06:07] Diego Alvarez: We'll produce a per-token cost and per-session cost comparison in the runbook appendix.
[06:12] Speaker 6: question about telemetry retention
[06:15] Samir Rao: How long do we retain raw telemetry? We might need 90 days for audit.
[06:20] Maya Chen: By default we store 30 days but enterprise retention add-ons can do 90/365. I'll include options and pricing in the follow-up.
[06:28] Leah Brooks: On the chaos test mechanics, Diego — will the test include node restarts that also simulate KV cache TTL expiry? We want to see both behavior.
[06:35] Diego Alvarez: Yes. The chaos job will evict KV entries, then randomly restart one worker, and also simulate a network pause on the control plane to exercise log lag scenarios. We'll capture traces, metrics, and the model response diffs.
[06:47] Ivan Gomez: We'll need the exact metrics exposed so our runbook can assert pass/fail. Can we get a metric list?
[06:53] Diego Alvarez: I'll paste that in the telemetry doc: p95 latency, p50, error rate, dropped tokens, fallback_count, kv_miss_rate, model_confidence_change.
[07:04] Ruth Patel: model_confidence_change — is that an internal number or something we can calculate from logits?
[07:09] Diego Alvarez: We expose a normalized confidence estimate on the response envelope; for deeper analysis you can export logits but that's an extra export. We'll flag that as optional.
[07:18] Maya Chen: All right, practical next steps: Diego will build the chaos test and share a scheduled window; Ivan will prep staging creds and a sanitized replay; Leah will finalize canary acceptance criteria; Maya will send the runbook and compliance docs. Anything else?
[07:31] Samir Rao: One last ask — we want to simulate an older quantized variant as part of the fallback so we can measure quality delta ahead of time.
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: That's doable — we'll bake that into the chaos job.
[07:41] Leah Brooks: Also request: daily digest during the A/B week with the top 3 regressions.
[07:46] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll set up an automated daily report and a Slack channel for alerts.
[07:50] Ruth Patel: Great. If we can get the runbook by Wednesday, we'll be able to schedule a rehearsal Friday.
[07:56] Maya Chen: We'll aim for that.
[08:00] (Cross talk, planning dates)
[08:12] Diego Alvarez: I'll also include a short checklist for the dry-run operator: cert checks, time sync, preflight load test, abort criteria, and post-test debrief notes.
[08:24] Ivan Gomez: For debrief, we want a post-mortem template so we can capture what failed vs expected.
[08:30] Maya Chen: We'll include a PM template.
[08:32] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[08:35] Maya Chen: Anything else from anyone?
[08:38] Ruth Patel: No, thanks. Good plan.
[08:41] Leah Brooks: No, thanks.
[08:43] Samir Rao: All good.
[08:45] Maya Chen: OK, recap of next steps and I'll send notes. Thanks everyone.
